chunks: In the Book of Ali (peace be upon him): When the eye blinks, or the foot kicks, or the tail moves, then eat from it, for you have realised its ritual slaughter.

key_terms.ذَكَاة: Dhakah — ritual slaughter that renders an animal lawful for consumption; also used to refer to the completion of the slaughter
key_terms.طَرَفَتِ الْعَيْنُ: The blinking of the eye — movement indicating the animal was alive at slaughter
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali — a compiled collection of rulings narrated from Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (AS), preserved among the Imams

ai.seo_question: What are the signs of valid ritual slaughter (dhakah) according to Imam al-Sadiq in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) cites a ruling from the Book of Ali (AS) concerning the validity of slaughter: if an animal shows signs of life after being cut — blinking, kicking, or moving its tail — this confirms the slaughter was performed correctly while the animal was still alive, and the meat is permissible to eat. This ruling addresses a practical concern in Islamic jurisprudence about distinguishing a lawful slaughter (dhakah) from an animal that was already dead, since consuming carrion (maytah) is forbidden. The three signs given — eye movement, leg movement, and tail movement — serve as observable indicators that the animal's vital functions were still active at the moment of slaughter.
